episodes.165681: A low pressure system dropped southward off the California coast on March 3 then turned inland and moved across southern California during the morning of March 4 spreading moderate to locally heavy precipitation into the south San Joaquin Valley with localized street flooding being observed in the Bakersfield area. Light precipitation impacted the Tehachapi Mountains with the snow level lowering from 5000 feet at the onset of the precipitation to 4000 feet by the evening of March 4.  A colder system then dropped southward along the California Nevada border on March 5 which pushed a cold front southward through the area bringing mainly light precipitation to much of our area and lowering the snow level to around 2000 feet.  Snowfall was generally 3 to 6 inches of above 5000 feet and 1 to 3 inches between 2500 feet and 5000 feet.  The snow did result in traffic being paced along Interstate 5 over the Tejon Pass for a few hours on March 5 and briefly closed a few roads in the Kern County Mountains as some precautionary measures were taken.  Parts of the south San Joaquin Valley picked up between 0.75 inches and 1.5 inches of rainfall, but further north the the central valley most locations picked up between a quarter and a half inch of rainfall.
episodes.165948: A closed midlevel low pressure system lifted across the Four Corners region. An uptick in moisture and support aloft paired with marginal instability resulted in isolated thunderstorms in southwest Colorado. One storm produced gusty winds of up to 58 mph at the Cortez Municipal Airport.
episodes.166631: With the migrating upper level low, the moist boundary layer and cool air aloft lead to conditions prime for funnel formation.
episodes.167261: Two closed upper low pressure systems produced widespread precipitation, high-elevation snow and lightning from March 3 to 6. The first system occurred on March 3, producing strong winds across the mountains and deserts, scattered thunderstorms, and light snow in the mountains. The second, colder system, occurred March 5 and 6, and produced heavier snow in the San Bernardino and San Diego County Mountains.

events.narrative: California Highway Patrol reported that the intersection of SR 184 and Redbank Rd. in Bakersfield was completely flooded.
Trained spotter reported rainfall of 0.68 inch 2 WSW El Cajon. Rain started at 1:50 AM.
NWS employee reported 1.20 inch of rain via Davis Pro Weather Station. About 10 lightning strikes from 2 to 3 AM.
A peak wind gust of 58 MPH was measured by the automated weather station at the Cortez Municipal Airport.
A cold core funnel was spotted near Lewiston Hill by several public sources. The location was estimated based on reports and pictures. It did not impact people or property.
